result.topic_en: Conclusion of the problem: the first integral P = C gives p, hence the differential equation of the curve, which agrees with the earlier result, illustrating how a slight transformation makes hard problems easy.
result.transcription:
42
M plane in computum non ingreditur, cum aequatio pro
curva quaesita sit $N\partial x = \partial P$, sive $\partial P = 0$, unde statim
sequitur $P = \frac{wpxx}{\sqrt{(1+ppxx)}} = C$, quae ipsa aequatio naturam
curvae jam declarat.

45. Ex hac autem aequatione elicimus $p = \frac{c}{x\sqrt{(wwxx - cc)}}$,
sicque ob $p = \frac{\partial y}{\partial x}$ erit $\partial y = \int \frac{c\,\partial x}{x\sqrt{wwx^2 - cc}}$, quae aequatio
perfecte cum ea congruit, quam ante per tantas ambages
sumus consecuti, si modo loco $x$ hic restituamus $v$, tum
vero noster angulus, hic $y$ vocatus, idem erit, quem ante
designavimus littera $\phi$. Ex hoc exemplo intelligitur, quo-
modo saepenumero problemata in se difficillima per levem
transformationem solutu facillima reddi queant.

items.english: This equation agrees perfectly with the one we obtained earlier through so many detours, provided we put v back in place of x here.

items.quote:
Ex hoc exemplo intelligitur, quo-
modo saepenumero problemata in se difficillima per levem
transformationem solutu facillima reddi queant.
items.english: From this example one understands how problems that are very difficult in themselves can often be made very easy to solve by a slight transformation.
